focus: Parallelism and concurrency: concurrency groups, cancel-in-progress, matrix, fail-fast and needs across all 33 workflows, plus the carried-forward vitest fileParallelism question
answeredQuestions: Are parallelism, matrix design, fail-fast and concurrency cancel-in-progress groups set well?

graphEvents.label: Are parallelism, matrix, fail-fast and concurrency groups set well?
32 of 33 workflows have no concurrency group
206 superseded push runs ran to completion, 534 wall-min exposure
15 of 22 workflows self-overlap, peak 4 concurrent runs
Wall clock sits in one serial job, not the job graph
Matrix minimal, fail-fast never true, dual-version provisions three times
fileParallelism false repo-wide, sharding is the lever
Trigger Index Rebuild group is the correct exception
Cancel-in-progress on main trades verification for speed

label: Only 1 of 33 workflows declares concurrency (trigger-index-rebuild.yml:21-23, cancel-in-progress:false); the other 32 have no concurrency key, so a second push to the same branch starts a full parallel run of every workflow.

206 of 1000 runs in the 23.5h window are push runs that started while an earlier push run of the same workflow on the same branch was in flight; 204 concluded success, i.e. they ran to completion after being logically superseded, with 534 wall-clock minutes of exposure that cancel-in-progress would remove.

15 of the 22 workflow names in the window reached same-workflow peak concurrency above 1 (peak 4 for Spec-Kit Check, sk-doc Script Tests, Hook Node Tests, Message Contract, Playbook Operator Contract and Command Tree Parity); global peak was 45 concurrent runs with median 10 and median queue delay 0s, so redundancy rather than runner capacity is the constraint.

spec-kit-check's three jobs already run in parallel with no needs, and its wall clock is one serial check job of install+build+typecheck+shared tests+ripgrep+CLI vitest+legacy lanes+runtime vitest at 1215s median vs 62s and 163s for the sibling jobs; deep-loop-runtime (688s) and hooks-node-tests (194s) are likewise single serial jobs.

No unnecessary needs: chains exist - the only two are trigger-index-rebuild push->rebuild (artifact and outputs dependency) and pi-extension-tests matrix->discover (dynamic matrix), so every multi-job workflow already parallelises its jobs; the parallelism deficit is across runs and inside single jobs.

Only 2 of 33 workflows use a matrix (opencode-dual-version matrix.include, pi-extension-tests fromJSON) and neither uses fail-fast:true; the dual-version legs each run provision_worktree and the both job provisions a third time, so matrix parallelism multiplies setup work threefold.

fileParallelism:false is set in every substantive vitest config (spec-kit runtime line 38 with a shared-state and temp-root WHY, spec-kit root line 50 and cli line 67, deep-loop runtime line 20 for the graph writer lock, skill-advisor runtime line 39 and stress line 25), so the carried-forward question is answered and worker parallelism is not an available lever - suite sharding across runners is.

trigger-index-rebuild must keep cancel-in-progress:false: its own comments document that the group keeps one run in progress plus one pending, a newer pending run replaces an older one, and a rejected push exits 0 because the newer run rebuilds on the newer tip; cancelling there would drop rebuilds, so its 61.6 min of superseded exposure is push cadence, not a missing group.

Cancel-in-progress on push-to-main leaves the superseded commit with no conclusion for that workflow, which matters where a required status check binds to a push run; the safe default is a per-workflow per-ref group that always cancels pull_request runs and cancels push runs only on unprotected refs.

Only six jobs declare timeout-minutes (deep-loop-runtime 45, opencode-dual-version 30/30, skill-advisor-stress 20, hooks-node-tests 20, sk-doc-rename-harness 30, opencode-plugin-tests 20); every other job inherits GitHub's 360-minute default, so without a concurrency group a hung job on main holds a runner for up to six hours.

direction: Enable vitest fileParallelism:true (or raise maxWorkers) to shorten the long suite jobs
reason: Every substantive config disables file parallelism deliberately, with in-file reasons naming shared process state, temp project roots and the graph writer lock; flipping it trades a deterministic suite for flaky failures and does not reduce the install cost that dominates the job.

direction: Introduce needs: to serialise or reorder existing multi-job workflows
reason: Only two needs: exist and both are real data dependencies (rebuild artifact handoff, dynamic matrix discovery); every other multi-job workflow already runs its jobs concurrently, so there is no serial chain to break.

direction: Set fail-fast:true on opencode-dual-version's battery matrix
reason: The workflow states that each OpenCode family reports on its own and a failure in one must not cancel the other; fail-fast:true would hide the v2 result when v1 fails, so the level of failure visibility is intentional.
